section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion summarizes psychometric support for the 10-item BAS-2 across three studies involving college and online community (MTurk) women and men from the U.S., noting its unidimensionality, reliability, validity, and measurement invariance. It reports that BAS-2 scores relate adaptively to other well-being and eating measures, that BAS-2 is inversely related to BMI (moderately) across samples, and that Study 2 specifically found differences in BAS-2 scores between college men and women and between college and community men.
